say: Here's how to fly past four planets, starting in your garage.
Step one. Buy a Titan Three E Centaur rocket. It's sixteen stories tall, so... measure the garage.
Step two. Solar panels won't cut it out by Neptune, so grab three plutonium generators. Normal garage stuff.
Step three. A computer with sixty nine kilobytes of memory. That's smaller than one selfie.
Step four. A golden record. Whale songs, and Chuck Berry, in case aliens like rock and roll.
Step five. Wait for the planets to line up. It only happens every hundred and seventy five years.
Step six. Roll it to your backyard. Ideally, your backyard is Cape Canaveral.
August twentieth, nineteen seventy seven. Boosters, two Titan stages, Centaur, kick motor. Bye, Earth.
Jupiter. Swing past and steal some of its speed. That's a gravity assist.
Uranus. Nobody had ever been here. Nobody has since.
Neptune. Its moon Triton is shooting geysers.
Then keep going. Forty nine years later, over thirteen billion miles out, it's still flying.
Last step. Tell your neighbors it was a weather balloon.
